patch.value: Adopt --respect-item-release in changelog scripts and bump pm-changelog to 2026.7.24

pm-changelog 2026.7.24 adds --respect-item-release, which makes the single-window generation path (--since-previous-tag --until-release-tag, changelog:check, release notes) honour an item's declared release field instead of trusting closed_at. Without it, closing a tracker whose fix shipped in an earlier release dates months-old work as new, which is why shipped-but-unclosed trackers accumulate: closing them corrupts the changelog. Adopting the flag fleet-wide makes late tracker closure safe and keeps every package's generation path in agreement with --all-release-tags.

changelog, changelog:full, changelog:check and release:notes all pass --respect-item-release; pm-changelog devDependency is ^2026.7.24; npm run changelog:check is green; CHANGELOG.md content is unchanged by the flag for this repo (no item declares a release yet)

value.author: claude
value.text: Verified in this repo: pm-changelog 2026.7.24 installed; npm run changelog:full regenerated CHANGELOG.md with the flag active and produced a ZERO-line diff, confirming the flag is a safe no-op until an item declares a release; npm run changelog:check exits 0.

patch.value: Work completed and released in 2026.7.24. Release attribution set explicitly so pm-changelog --respect-item-release files the entry under 2026.7.24 instead of the current release notes.
A closed item whose changelog entry appears under the 2026.7.24 heading it actually shipped in, leaving the current release notes untouched.
Item remained in_progress with no activity after its work shipped, so the delivery was absent from the changelog while still counting as open work in every fleet audit.

Retired as shipped: adopting --respect-item-release in the changelog scripts was completed and released in 2026.7.24, but the item was never closed and sat in progress ever since, inflating every fleet audit.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: Release attribution corrected to 2026.7.25 after review. The first attribution used the item's last-activity DATE, which is unsound: an item can be touched before the release that finally carried its code. Verified instead by tag containment — git tag --contains f544e4c reports 2026.7.25 as the first release holding the implementation commit. Greptile caught this on PR #67 by noticing a historical release predating its implementation.

patch.value: Before this closeout the item had remained in_progress with no activity since its work shipped, so the delivery was missing from the changelog while still being counted as open work in every fleet audit. Closing it with an explicit release attribution is what added the historical entry.
A closed item whose changelog entry appears under the 2026.7.25 heading, the first release actually containing f544e4c, leaving the current release notes untouched.

Work completed and released in 2026.7.25. Release attribution verified by containment rather than by date: git merge-base --is-ancestor f544e4c v2026.07.25 succeeds, so 2026.7.25 is the first release whose tree holds the implementing commit. An earlier revision of this record said 2026.7.24; that came from matching the item's last-activity DATE to a release and is superseded.

Retired as shipped: adopting --respect-item-release in the changelog scripts was completed and released in 2026.7.25, verified by tag containment against implementing commit f544e4c. The item was never closed and sat in progress ever since, inflating every fleet audit.
